correctness.rationale: The published \(3n\)-vertex list is specialized explicitly. Direct LPs reproduce the support formula in 300 independent seeded directions. An explicit Gaussian union-bound estimate makes every \(k\ge2\) row mean negligible at \(n^{-1/2}(\log n)^{-3/4}\) scale. Two correlated columns are removed with cost O(1/(n sqrt(log n))); an independent integral has a Gamma(1/2) Laplace limit \(\pi^{1/4}/2\) per singleton, giving \(\pi^{1/4}\) in Gaussian support and sqrt(2) \(\pi^{1/4}\) in intrinsic mean width. Gaussian polar decomposition and the standard maxima limit complete the result. Quantifiers are \(n\ge3\) for finite statements, \(n\to\infty\) for limits; finite checks corroborate rather than certify.

value.rationale: The exact secondary-order deficit is a natural geometric quantity between a canonical Monge cost-matrix polytope and its distinguished column-vertex simplex. The full polytope and simplex have the same leading sqrt(2 log n/n) width, but exactly two exceptional row singleton vertices generate the nontrivial positive \(n^{-1}(\log n)^{-3/4}\) correction with an explicit coefficient. This identifies the first scale invisible to the Gumbel limit and the complete \(3n\)-vertex support formula, a motivated asymptotic invariant rather than a routine finite computation.
